title: Linear–quadratic systems
examples: How do I use substitution when one equation is squared?
What does it mean when the discriminant is zero in this context?
Can you show me an example where the line just touches the curve?

explain.say: Today we look at systems with a line and a curve. We use substitution to solve these together.
Take the equation y equals x squared plus one. And the line y equals two x. We set them equal to each other.
So we write x squared plus one equals two x. Now we must move everything to one side. This gives us x squared minus two x plus one equals zero.
We solve this quadratic for x. Factoring gives us x minus one times x minus one equals zero. This means x equals one is our only solution.
This single solution means the line touches the curve at only one point. This is called tangency. We can check this with the discriminant later.

faq.q: What do the solutions mean for the graph?
faq.a: The solutions you find are the x coordinates where the line and the curve meet. Graphically, these are the points of intersection.
asks: What do the intersection points represent?

faq.q: When should I use the discriminant?
faq.a: You use the discriminant when you have already substituted and ended up with a quadratic equation. It tells you about the number of solutions.
asks: Do I always need the discriminant?

faq.q: What does a negative discriminant mean?
faq.a: A negative discriminant means there are no real solutions for x. This implies the line and the curve never touch each other.
asks: If the discriminant is negative, what happens?
Does a negative value mean no intersection?

faq.q: How do I find the point of tangency?
faq.a: First, use substitution to get the quadratic. Then, set the discriminant to zero to find the required relationship between the line and the curve.
asks: How do I find the tangent point?
What is the process for tangency?

faq.q: Can I solve this without substitution?
faq.a: It is much harder to solve without substitution. Substitution is the standard method for combining these two types of equations.
asks: Is there another way to solve this system?

facts: Substitution involves replacing one variable in one equation with an expression from the other equation.
The discriminant, found in b squared minus four a c, tells us the number of real solutions for a quadratic.
If the discriminant is positive, there are two intersection points. If it is zero, there is one point of tangency.
If the discriminant is negative, the line and the curve do not intersect at any real points.

quiz.say: If solving a system leads to x squared plus 3x minus 4 equals zero, how many solutions are there?
quiz.why: Factoring gives (x+4)(x-1)=0, so x=-4 and x=1. This means two intersection points.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the equation can be easily factored into real numbers.
wrong.1: This is incorrect because the highest power of x is two, limiting the number of solutions.
wrong.3: This is tempting because the equation looks simple, but it is not a perfect square.

quiz.say: For the equation x squared plus 4x + 4 equals zero, what does the discriminant tell us?

options.show: The line is tangent to the curve
options.say: The line is tangent to the curve

quiz.why: A discriminant of zero means there is exactly one real solution, which indicates tangency.

wrong.1: This happens when the discriminant is negative, not zero.
wrong.2: This happens when the discriminant is a positive number.
wrong.3: The discriminant only relates to the number of solutions, not the line's orientation.

quiz.say: If the discriminant of the resulting quadratic is minus nine, what is the relationship between the line and the curve?

options.show: The line crosses the curve twice
options.say: The line crosses the curve twice

options.show: The line is parallel to the curve
options.say: The line is parallel to the curve

options.show: The line does not intersect the curve
options.say: The line does not intersect the curve

options.show: The line is tangent to the curve
options.say: The line is tangent to the curve

quiz.why: A negative discriminant means there are no real values for x that satisfy the equation, so no intersection exists.

wrong.0: Crossing twice requires the discriminant to be a positive number.
wrong.1: Parallelism is a concept related to slopes, not the discriminant value.
wrong.3: Tangency requires the discriminant to be exactly zero.
